In this section, you are expected to describe an overview of your idea of the DBMS you want to design and develop, what are the business questions based on what you will cover in your system. You will need a good logical relational database management system representation (ERD) based on your proposed idea. This includes Formal Data Modelling with detailed features of your system.  
Your submission must be a single report (PDF) and should contain: 
• Business system summary based on the chosen topic. 
• Describe your business idea in detail. 
• Describe work objectives.
• An ERD (logical schema) of your proposed idea using an appropriate tool (It is required that you ERD contains 12-14 distinguish Entity sets in it).  
• Indicate key attribute for each entity set. 
• Indicate cardinality for each relationship. 
• Indicate participation for each entity related to each relationship.

• A diagram (physical data model) which fully match the ERD, should clearly shows:  
• All tables 
• Columns within each table 
• Constraints including data types and Keys (Primary Key and Foreign Key) 
Deliverables (what you will need to submit): a single report (PDF) 
Additional Information: 
To properly design your business database, you may need to perform some literature review. If you have used ideas from anywhere other than the lecture notes and tutorial examples (e.g., from a book, the Internet, or a fellow student) then include a reference showing where ideas came from and label your content carefully to show which parts are borrowed.  
Please be aware that diagrams in your submission must be fully original.

To achieve maximum success in this task: 
• Select a suitable business idea that clearly requires a relational database (complex data, multiple entities, clear relationships). 
• Define clear objectives and key business questions your system will address. 
• Develop a detailed and accurate ERD with 12–14 entities, showing primary keys, relationships, cardinality, and participation. 
• Create a consistent physical data model that fully matches your ERD, including tables, data types, and key constraints. 
• Present a professional, well-structured report (single PDF) with clear sections and original, well-labelled diagrams. 
• Demonstrate professionalism through clear communication, correct referencing, and attention to detail.

Students do not need another resource, book, article to complete this assignment. In case they use another online/offline resource, they must cite it in the References section, at the end of the report. 
If you do so, please use IEEE style: https://www.citethemrighttutorial.com/course-modules/ieee

This assessment has been designed to provide you with an opportunity to demonstrate your achievement of the following skills, which are critical in professional contexts and employment settings. 
By successfully completing this assessment, you will be able to: 
• Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to translate business requirements into effective database designs. 
• Use equivalent industry-standard tools and techniques to develop Entity Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) and physical data models. 
• Demonstrate attention to detail and accuracy in data modelling and documentation. 
• Communicate technical concepts clearly and professionally in a business context.

The assessment is designed so that the use of AI during the assessment is irrelevant or impossible. You are welcome to use AI to support learning and preparation for this assessment. Please make sure you read and understand the assessment guidelines and ask your Module Leader if you have any questions.  
You can find the guidance on the use of AI by using the following link.
